properties.title: NOAH: Learning the Full Patient Journey. A Longitudinal Multimodal Time-Aware Model for Representation and Forecasting

properties.version_basis: PDF identified by SHA-256 against assignments.json; title page read.

properties.description: Generative multimodal time-aware patient trajectory model evaluated retrospectively on MIMIC.

Causal transformer over timestamped multimodal events with a variational latent patient state, frozen external encoders for images, text, ECG and echo, autoregressive rollout and Monte Carlo readouts.

properties.algorithm: Causal transformer with context-conditional variational latent and component decoders

properties.population: MIMIC family patients (ICU, ED, ward, notes, CXR, ECG, echo)
properties.decision: forecasting, outcome estimation and fluid-intervention simulation (research)

properties.description: 1,085 sepsis patients for the saline versus Ringer's simulation
Patient-level test split of the merged MIMIC records (70/15/15)
Retrospective forecasting, zero-shot, counterfactual, probing and survival evaluations on held-out MIMIC patients

properties.algorithm: NOAH with time control (ground truth time delta supplied)

assertions.rationale: Merged MIMIC subsets with event construction, windows and minimum-token rules are described, with dataset statistics in tables outside the text read.
Every record is a timestamped event on a lifetime timeline.
No separate availability time is described.
No missing-data indicator is described in the text read, and missing demographics fall back to Unknown.

criteria_met: Inter-event time deltas enter the model as inputs
criteria_missing: A test of robustness to irregular sampling

assertions.rationale: No harmonization across the MIMIC subsets beyond a subject-ID merge is described.
A patient-level split places every patient in one split.
Frozen external encoders map images, text, ECG and echo to embeddings that feed a trained projection.
Pretrained RAD-DINO, BioLORD, OTIS and EchoPrime embeddings are reused.
Next-event components are predicted from a latent state.
No collapse control is described in the text read.
No reconstruction test of the external encoders is reported.
Event type, specifics, value and time are combined into one token in a shared space.

A 768-dimensional causal transformer patient state h_t and variational latent z_t are carried across events and autoregressively updated in implemented MIMIC experiments (559M training events, 13,551 test patients; pp. 5, 16, 20-21, 35).

criteria_met: Two fluid arms are simulated and compared

assertions.rationale: Next-event prediction conditioned on prior patient state h_{t-1} and bidirectional inter-event time deltas is implemented and evaluated across 1-72 h horizons on 13,551 held-out MIMIC test patients (pp. 16-17, 20-21, 35).
The causal transformer, variational prior/posterior, and cascading multimodal decoders are trained end-to-end via ELBO on 559M MIMIC events using Muon and AdamW (pp. 16, 20-21).
The treatment event conditions the rollout and outcomes are compared, with the authors stating the output is an intervention-conditioned forecast.
A sampled prior gives varied trajectories and calibration of the resulting probabilities is reported.
No mechanistic component is combined with the learned transition.
Training predicts one token ahead and the authors name this as a limit.
No hierarchy of timescales is described.
Component heads decode type, time and value embeddings from the latent.
Linear probes, a NEWS2 regressor and survival readouts use the state.

Autoregressive future clinical event-type and modality occurrence predictions are evaluated against held-out ground truth across 1, 6, 24, and 72 h horizons on 13,551 MIMIC test patients (Extended Data Table 1, p. 35; Methods, p. 21), satisfying the ontology definition of rollout.one_step_evaluated (future-state prediction evaluated), although isolated single-token next-step metrics are not separately tabulated.
Autoregressive rollouts to 72 h are scored against held-out events and a persistence baseline.
No reassimilation during rollouts is described.
Horizons of 1 to 72 h and 30 days are reported.
Error growth with horizon is reported and attributed to drift.
Fifty or 25 sampled rollouts per patient give Monte Carlo probabilities.

evidence_fragments.content: [paraphrase of Extended Data Table 1, p. 35] Macro AUROC and Brier score at 1, 6, 24 and 72 h for event types (C=31) and modalities (C=6), N=13,551 patients, 95 percent patient-bootstrap intervals. Event-type AUROC at 1/6/24/72 h: persistence 0.582/0.627/0.610/0.592; NOAH free 0.747/0.826/0.829/0.820; NOAH time-controlled 0.866/0.854/0.856/0.842. Modality AUROC: persistence 0.657/0.604/0.583/0.571; free 0.764/0.818/0.811/0.813; time-controlled 0.952/0.894/0.839/0.828. Event-type Brier: persistence 0.059/0.119/0.274/0.377; free 0.045/0.073/0.092/0.105; time-controlled 0.032/0.061/0.089/0.110. Modality Brier: persistence 0.091/0.147/0.147/0.174; free 0.097/0.101/0.094/0.087; time-controlled 0.038/0.075/0.092/0.084.

Effect saline minus Ringer's +8.86 pp (+4.30 pp over all runs); SMART sepsis subgroup +4.9 pp (+0.4, +9.2). Hospital LOS hours: observed 253.7, matched 170.1, saline 174.3, Ringer's 135.7, effect +40.5.

capability_assessments.rationale: A learned latent patient model is rolled out autoregressively and scored on held-out MIMIC patients, and a fluid event conditions the rollout with arm outcomes compared. L3 is not claimed because the authors state the simulations are intervention-conditioned forecasts and not causal modelling, the simulated effect is about twice the trial subgroup magnitude, and no identification or support analysis is reported.

gate_assessments.rationale: Patient-level 70/15/15 splits, end-of-event tokens at charted termination, and readmission prompt truncation reduce leakage, but pretraining overlap between frozen external encoders (RAD-DINO, BioLORD, OTIS, EchoPrime) and the MIMIC test split is unaudited, and training window demographic prefixes use the latest value at window end (p. 15); downgraded from pass to unresolved.

Held-out forecasts over 1-72 h beat persistence, but evaluation outcomes are mixed (30-day readmission AUROC 0.609 with 64.5% scorable rollout coverage, increasing type-count MAE at longer horizons under time control, and unaudited external-encoder overlap); downgraded from pass to unresolved.

Horizons from 1 to 72 h and 30 days are evaluated and drift is observed, but no tolerance-defined effective usable horizon is declared (rollout.effective_horizon is not_reported, assertion:B062:0059); downgraded from pass to unresolved.
Only two fluid arms are compared and no overlap or support analysis of fluid choice is reported.

notes:
NOAH is a causal transformer over lifetime multimodal MIMIC event sequences with a variational latent patient state, trained on 299k patients with a patient-level split. Autoregressive Monte Carlo rollouts forecast event and modality occurrence (AUROC 0.83 to 0.95 by horizon against a persistence baseline), zero-shot outcomes (mortality AUROC 0.97, readmission 0.61) and a saline versus Ringer's simulation whose sign matches the SMART sepsis subgroup at about twice the magnitude, with strong mortality overprediction. Classified L2, core. Source points: retrospective single-source data, no causal identification, exposure bias, code only promised.
